subcategory: hallucination detection guardrail for RAG (small reasoning model)
task: Classify document-claim pairs as grounded or hallucinated and justify the decision
problem: RAG pipelines still hallucinate; large LLM judges are costly, while compact detectors rarely give evidence-grounded justifications.
architecture: HalluGuard: Qwen3-4B small reasoning model fine-tuned with LoRA and ORPO on synthetic preference data. Data pipeline: FineWeb documents curated and stylistically reformed by Qwen3-235B-A22B, synthetic grounded / intrinsic / extrinsic hallucinated claims, preference pairs from a large (chosen) vs small (rejected) generator, filtered by model agreement and LLM consensus.
retriever: not applicable (post-hoc verifier of RAG outputs against supplied documents)
generator: Qwen3-4B (detector); Qwen3-235B-A22B / Qwen3-0.6B used for data generation
knowledge_source: documents supplied with each claim (closed-book document-grounded setting)

datasets.name: LLM-AggreFact
datasets.details: 11 human-annotated grounding datasets, binary grounded vs hallucinated

datasets.name: FineWeb
datasets.details: training source; 300,000 sampled documents reduced to 104,966 after curation

key_results: Average LLM-AggreFact BAcc 77.1 vs 75.9 for GPT-4o and 75.7 for the Qwen3-4B backbone; MiniCheck averages 77.4.
Paired permutation test reports a significant advantage over MiniCheck in expected BAcc (+0.81, p < 0.001).
strengths: 4B detector competitive with 7-8B specialised detectors and much larger general LLMs; produces justifications.
Training data built without human annotation; datasets and model released.

limitations.text: Synthetic claims may not capture the complexity of real-world hallucinations, limiting generalisation.
Only a three-label taxonomy (grounded, intrinsic, extrinsic) is used.
Trained and evaluated only on English; legal or financial domains untested.

notes: Gain on RAGTruth over the backbone is modest (84.4 vs 84.0).
title: HalluGuard: Evidence-Grounded Small Reasoning Models to Mitigate Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
